prompt:
Create a brand-new ORIGINAL production game sprite atlas for ASHVEIL: the CINDER BEAR, a 340 kg four-legged bear from a cold ash-covered post-disaster highland. No existing game sprites, no tracing. The art must be exceptionally detailed, crisp hand-clustered pixel art with restrained 2-3 pixel texture clusters, hard readable silhouettes, warm soot-brown underfur and charcoal-black singed fur tips, subtle desaturated grey ash on the shoulder hump. Small ROUND ears, a broad short brown-bear muzzle, small dark amber eyes, black nose, very heavy chest and rump, four thick anatomically jointed legs with broad clawed paws, tiny stub tail. This is unmistakably a heavy grizzly-like BEAR, never a wolf, dog, hog or humanoid. No armor, flames, glowing eyes, magic, equipment or accessories. Natural muted lighting with readable material detail; not blurry photorealism, not smooth vector art, not a cute cartoon.

ATLAS CONTRACT: one square 1024 by 1024 transparent RGBA PNG, EXACTLY 4 equal rows by 4 equal columns. One fully separated whole-body sprite per 256x256 cell, 16 sprites total. At least 25 pixels of true transparent empty spacing around each silhouette. No contact shadows, floor, scenery, labels, text, grid lines, checkered background, borders or stray marks. Same bear identity, body mass, head size, camera elevation and lighting in every cell. Camera: consistent elevated 3/4 game view, not isometric scenery.

Each row has ONLY ONE direction: row 1 faces FRONT toward the bottom edge (show bear face, left/right paws foreshortened and hind legs behind); row 2 faces LEFT toward the left edge (nose at left, tail at right); row 3 faces RIGHT toward the right edge (nose at right, tail at left); row 4 faces BACK toward the top edge (bear rump and tiny tail nearest viewer, face hidden). Keep that row order exactly; do not repeat front as back or left as right.

This atlas is IDLE only. Across the four columns draw FOUR distinct subtle anatomical poses in a looping breathing/alertness sequence: 1 neutral heavy planted stance, 2 chest inhale and muzzle raised slightly, 3 chest expanded with small ear/head attention shift, 4 exhale and muzzle lowered slightly. All four paws stay on the ground, but the torso/head silhouette must actually change between frames; do not paste the same sprite four times. Four real unique frames for each of the four directions. Keep the local ground-contact point/foot baseline steady within each row. Preserve enough paw separation to read four legs where they are visible, while allowing natural occlusion in front/back view. Full bear entirely inside each cell, no clipping, no extra legs or duplicated heads.
